                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       CelliD is a clustering-free multivariate statistical\nmethod for the robust extraction of per-cell gene signatures\nfrom single-cell RNA-seq. CelliD allows unbiased cell identity\nrecognition across different donors, tissues-of-origin, model\norganisms and single-cell omics protocols. The package can also\nbe used to explore functional pathways enrichment in single\ncell data.
#> 435                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) provides\nlong-term storage and controlled sharing of personally\nidentifiable genetic data. The Rega package offers a\nstreamlined and extensible R interface to the EGA API,\nfacilitating the programmatic upload of metadata. GEO-like\nExcel submission template is provided as a default method of\norganizing submission metadata.
#> 436                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      CPSM provides a comprehensive computational pipeline for\npredicting survival probability and risk groups in cancer\npatients. The package includes steps for data preprocessing,\ntraining/test split, and normalization. It enables feature\nselection using univariate survival analysis and computes a\nLASSO-based prognostic index (PI) score. CPSM supports the\ndevelopment of predictive models using various feature sets and\noffers a suite of visualization tools, including survival\ncurves based on predicted probabilities, barplots for predicted\nmean and median survival times, KM plots overlaid with\nindividual survival predictions, and nomograms for estimating\n1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year survival probabilities. This makes CPSM\na versatile tool for survival analysis in cancer research.

#> 39                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   igblastr 1.1.26\n\nAdd the following built-in germline dbs:\n\no _OGRDB.mouse.CAST_EiJ.IGH+IGK+IGL.202603\n\n  Contains sequences from OGRDB germline sets:\n    - `CAST/EiJ IGH` version 2\n    - `CAST/EiJ IGKV` version 1\n    - `CAST/EiJ IGLV` version 2\n    - `IGKJ (all strains)` version 1\n    - `IGLJ (all strains)` version 1\n\no _OGRDB.mouse.LEWES_EiJ.IGH+IGK+IGL.202603\n\n  Contains sequences from OGRDB germline sets:\n    - `LEWES/EiJ IGH` version 2\n    - `LEWES/EiJ IGKV` version 1\n    - `LEWES/EiJ IGLV` version 1\n    - `IGKJ (all strains)` version 1\n    - `IGLJ (all strains)` version 1\n\no _OGRDB.mouse.MSM_MsJ.IGH+IGK+IGL.202603\n\n  Contains sequences from OGRDB germline sets:\n    - `MSM/MsJ IGH` version 1\n    - `MSM/MsJ IGKV` version 1\n    - `MSM/MsJ IGLV` version 2\n    - `IGKJ (all strains)` version 1\n    - `IGLJ (all strains)` version 1\n\nAlso rename the following built-in germline dbs:\n\no _OGRDB.mouse.NOD_ShiLtJ.IGH+IGK+IGL.202501 (original name)\n  --> _OGRDB.mouse.NOD_ShiLtJ.IGH+IGK+IGL.202205 (new name)\n\no _OGRDB.mouse.PWD_PhJ.IGH+IGK+IGL.202501 (original name)\n  --> _OGRDB.mouse.PWD_PhJ.IGH+IGK+IGL.202410 (new name)\n\nThe new names better reflect the release date of the OGRDB germline sets\nthat they contain. The two original germline dbs were kept for backward\ncompatibility but the user gets a warning when they use them. The warning\nsuggests to use the new names instead and to remove the original dbs.\n

#> 82                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Update downsample logic for scuttle/tatami and fix tests (#129)\n\n* move to non-exact comparison\n\n* Updated downsampling C++ code to use new scuttle functions.\n\nAlso added some more checks to ensure we don't lose integer precision.\n\n* Stripped out test comparisons to downsampleMatrix.\n\nThese tests no longer make sense because the downsampling is no longer done on\na per-event basis (i.e. single UMIs or reads in each count). Rather, the new\nalgorithm operates on the entire count at once, for greater efficiency.\n\nThis all means that UMI and read counts are no longer interchangeable, which\nmeans that the results from downsampleReads/Matrix are no longer directly\ncomparable. This is okay - the test itself was highly contrived anyway as it\nonly works when every UMI has a single read.\n\n* Bumped version and date, updated NEWS.\n\n---------\n\nCo-authored-by: LTLA <infinite.monkeys.with.keyboards@gmail.com>
